titleEn: Pick It, Then Show Grandpa First!

pages.text: "Grandpa, there are lots of black berries here!" Nils the little bear crouched by a bush. The berries were round and shiny. Dry leaves lay thick on the autumn forest path.
"Today I will fill my basket!" Grandpa Bruno was picking berries from a bush up ahead. Nils plucked one black berry and popped it into his mouth.
Yuck—bitter! His tongue tingled and his mouth puckered. Nils spat, spat, spat. "Grandpa—! This one is strange!"
Grandpa strode over, took out his water bottle, and rinsed Nils's mouth. "This berry will give you a tummyache if you eat it. You spat it out quickly." Nils's cheeks grew hot.

Grandpa placed two berries side by side on his broad palm. "This one is for eating, and this one is not. Even I can confuse them just by looking." Nils peered closely, but they looked very much alike.

"That is why you show me first when you pick one." Nils plucked a berry and set it on Grandpa's palm. "What about this one?" "That one is for eating." His eyes sparkled. "Pick it, then show Grandpa first!"
Nils picked, showed, and put berries in his basket. Again: pick, show, put in. He left unfamiliar berries on their bushes. The basket filled up.
At a bend in the path, unfamiliar berries shone on a bush. Before, Nils would have grabbed them at once. Now he tucked both paws behind his back and called, "Grandpa—!"

Looking into his basket, Nils said three rules. "One, do not put unfamiliar things in your mouth! Two, show what you pick first! Three, if it seems strange, spit!" Then he raised both paws above his head. "Pick it, then show Grandpa first!"
Grandpa cradled Nils's head in his broad palm and touched noses with him. Ask first, rather than putting unfamiliar things in your mouth. "Grandpa, pick it, then show Grandpa first!"
